QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_8

question.text: SEBI requires investments held by Category I and Category II AIFs to be valued by:

answer.text: An independent valuer appointed by the AIF, using SEBI-specified methodologies, at least once every six months

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook (pp. 243-244), Regulation 23 requires that the AIF carry out valuation of its investments in the manner specified by SEBI. For Category I and Category II AIFs, investments must be valued by an independent valuer appointed by the AIF, and the valuation must be done at least once every six months. The independent valuer must meet the eligibility criteria laid down by SEBI. The Trap: The fund manager alone cannot self-value Cat I/II AIF investments; SEBI requires an independent valuer. The investee company's management is not the appointed valuer for the AIF's holdings. Distributors are sales intermediaries and have no valuation role under Regulation 23. Note: The independent-valuer-every-six-months rule on pp. 243-244 is specific to Category I and Category II AIF investments and is the standard framework under SEBI's valuation regulations.
